$comment: Single source of truth for the Questionnaire API. Every framework package is tested against this file.
name: questionnaire
title: Questionnaire
description: Multiple-choice questions the assistant asks inside a chat: one answer (radios) or several (checkboxes), an optional "Other" text box, Submit and Skip, and a read-only view once answered.
thumb:
How long a hike?

Half a dayA full day

questions.description: { id, prompt, hint?, multiple?, options: (string | { value, label })[], other?: boolean | string }. multiple uses checkboxes; other adds an "Other" option with a text box.

title / description.description: A heading above the questions; it names the form.

label.description: Name for the form when there's no title.

defaultValues / defaultOther.description: Chosen values ("other" for the Other option) and the typed Other text, by question id.

onSubmit.description: Answers by question id: a string, or a list for multiple. Other gives the typed text.
onSubmit.html: vinui.js fires vin-submit with detail.answers, keyed by each question's input name (add data-vin-questionnaire to the form)

state / defaultState.description: After Submit only the chosen answers stay, read-only; after Skip the questions fold away.
state / defaultState.html: data-state on the form, fieldsets disabled, p.vin-questionnaire__status[role=status]

examples.title: Basic
examples.description: One question with an "Other" text box that shows when you choose it. In HTML, add data-vin-questionnaire to the form.

examples.title: Several questions
examples.description: A title, a single-choice question and a choose-any question with Other filled in.

examples.title: Answered
examples.description: Read-only after Submit: only the chosen answer stays, with a note that it was sent.

a11y: Each question is a fieldset with its prompt as the legend, so screen readers read the question with every option.
Options are real radios and checkboxes: arrow keys move between radios, Space toggles checkboxes, and they work in forms without JavaScript.
The "Other" text box has its own label and only appears once Other is chosen.
After Submit or Skip, focus moves to the status line (role="status"), which says what happened; the answered questions stay readable but disabled.
